title: Introduce progressive soft-fail conductor with tenant-weighted backpressure and expiring leases
author: Priya Shah
description: Motivation: production incidents in high-variance tenant workloads exposed oscillations when the global SLO-enforcer flipped hard circuit states. This PR introduces a progressive soft-fail conductor that reduces instability by applying gradual tenant-weighted backpressure, expiring soft leases for temporary eviction, and a conservative rollout plan. Design summary: 1) Soft leases: when a tenant is selected for temporary degradation the conductor issues a short-lived "soft lease" (TTL) which lowers that tenant's available concurrency and grants a decay window before full eviction. Leases expire automatically and are tracked in memory and persisted to the local kv snapshot for fast reconnection. 2) Tenant-weighted backpressure: instead of absolute cutoffs, incoming requests are metered by a weight derived from tenant SLO slack and recent token-inflight cost. Higher weight => higher chance of acceptance; lower weight triggers request pacing with exponential jitter. 3) Progressive escalation: conductor transitions through states (normal -> metered -> soft-lease -> eviction) with configurable time and metric thresholds. State transitions include hysteresis to prevent flapping. 4) Telemetry: per-tenant metrics (soft_lease_active, lease_ttl_remaining_seconds, acceptance_weight, metered_rejects) and a debug trace event for each state change are emitted to the observability pipeline; we added sampling guards to limit cardinality. 5) Safety and rollback: defaults are conservative (short TTL, gentle weight slope, canary on 3% of traffic) and config is remote-overrideable via runtime flags. Migration and rollout: deploy conductor library to runtime nodes in canary (5%), then ramp to 25% with expanded telemetry retention, finally enable full roll. Provide an emergency kill-switch to revert to previous SLO-enforcer behavior. Tests and verification: unit tests for weight calc and lease expiry, integration tests that simulate bursty tenants with different SLO slacks, and an e2e canary harness that validates no more-than-1.5x latency tail increase for unaffected tenants. Why this is different from previous work: prior PRs implemented abrupt tenant eviction or aggressive circuit flips; this change introduces a measured intermediate lease layer with weights and temporal decay to reduce oscillations and improve user-visible continuity. Backwards compatibility notes: the conductor respects existing tenant config and opt-outs; feature is disabled by default and gated by runtime flags. Operational notes: new dashboards in Console -> Reliability -> Soft Fail Conductor show per-tenant lease state and a rollup of soft-lease capacity. Oncall runbook: steps to diagnose (check trace events, acceptance_weight histogram, lease TTLs), manual eviction extension, and emergency rollback steps are included in the attached docs.

release_notes: Added progressive soft-fail conductor: introduces tenant soft leases, tenant-weighted backpressure, and conservative rollout flags. Disabled by default. See docs/release_notes/754321-soft-fail-conductor.md for configuration examples and runbook.
manual_rollback_steps: 1) Toggle runtime flag soft_fail_conductor.enabled=false and wait for canary nodes to stop issuing leases. 2) Trigger coordinated node drain for any nodes stuck in metered state. 3) Revert runtime configuration if persistence schema was changed (apply backward migration). 4) Notify oncall and increase telemetry retention for 6h to validate stability.
notes_for_oncall: Key metrics: conductor.soft_lease_count, conductor.acceptance_weight_p50/p95, conductor.metered_rejects. Typical troubleshooting: high soft_lease_count + TTLs near zero indicates churn; lengthen TTL or reduce canary percentage. If unaffected tenants see increased tail latencies, immediately reduce canary percentage and engage rollback.
safety_considerations: Leases are short-lived by default (30s) and expire automatically. Persistence to local kv is used for quick resume but respects the LRU cap; a separate cleanup job periodically compacts stale lease entries. Sampling of trace events is capped to 1% to control cardinality. All parameters are tunable remotely and a kill-switch exists to restore prior SLO-enforcer behavior.
notes_for_releasemanager: Coordinate with Observability to ensure dashboard deployment (observability/dashboards/soft_fail_conductor.yaml) is applied during the canary phase. Communicate to SRE oncall about the new runbook. No database schema migrations required for central config; local snapshot format incremented (compatible).
